more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
Approved in the US.
US food use is subject to the listed CFR provisions and their conditions, checked in 2026.
more_info.overview: Lecithins are mixtures or fractions of phospholipids from edible plant or animal materials; the specifications also cover suitable enzyme-hydrolysed preparations. Its emulsifying role is to help form or maintain mixtures of oil and water in the finished food. Phospholipid mixtures are separated from vegetable or animal food materials. Some lecithins are further processed with enzymes. The specified material is supplied as brown powder or liquid.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain cocoa and Chocolate products as covered by Directive 2000/36/EC; other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; fruit juices as defined by Directive 2001/112/EC and vegetable juices; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.daily_intake: No numerical ADI needed for the assessed uses (EFSA, 2017).
more_info.origin: Phospholipid mixtures are separated from vegetable or animal food materials. Some lecithins are further processed with enzymes.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: The specification allows both animal and vegetable sources. Vegan, vegetarian and religious suitability therefore depend on the identified source of the particular lecithin preparation.
more_info.side_effects:
EFSA found no concern from reported food uses or their associated choline exposure.
The opinion does not establish safety for unlimited supplementary intake.
